item.title: The Relationship Between OCD and Eating Disorders: Understanding the Overlap and Impact
item.description: OCD and eating disorders frequently coexist, with shared patterns of intrusive thoughts and compulsive behaviors. This article explains why the two conditions overlap, how starvation can worsen OCD symptoms, and what integrated treatment approaches look like.

item.title: Understanding Eating Disorders: Identifying the Signs and Getting Help
item.description: Eating disorders are serious mental health conditions that impact eating behaviors, thoughts, and emotional well-being. This guide explains common types of eating disorders, how to distinguish normal eating from disordered patterns, and key signs that someone may be struggling.

item.title: The Neuroscience and Psychosocial Aspects of Eating Disorders
item.description: Eating disorders arise from a complex blend of brain-based factors, emotional patterns, genetics, and social influences. This article breaks down the neuroscience, behavioral mechanisms, and psychosocial components behind eating disorders, offering a comprehensive understanding of how these conditions develop.

item.title: Beyond the Ketamine Session: Innovative Integration for Lasting Healing
item.description: Ketamine therapy creates a powerful window of neuroplasticity, but integration is what turns insights into lasting change. This article explores innovative integration practices—from somatic work to VR—that help patients anchor transformation long after the session ends.

item.title: EMDR: A Revolutionary Approach to Trauma and Beyond
item.description: EMDR is a groundbreaking, evidence-based therapy that helps reprocess traumatic memories and reduce emotional distress. Learn how EMDR works, why it’s effective, and the wide range of conditions it can treat beyond trauma.

item.title: Grounding Techniques for Emotional Regulation
item.description: These therapist-developed grounding techniques use sensory engagement, movement, and mindful focus to help regulate overwhelming emotions and return to the present moment.

item.title: Common Myths About Eating Disorders
item.description: Eating disorders are surrounded by harmful myths that prevent people from getting the help they need. This article debunks eight common misconceptions and explains the reality of these complex conditions.

item.title: Effective Ways to Break the Cycle of Self-Sabotage
item.description: Self-sabotage can keep you stuck in painful patterns. This guide offers therapist-informed tools to recognize your behaviors, build self-awareness, challenge fears, and create empowering habits for lasting change.
